answer: Each hollow, an agent identity, gets influence equal to the square of its locked ferrous × epochs held, where ferrous is a staked token. The anchor, a public ledger, tracks every ferrous unit's lock lineage, so ferrous moved to another hollow restarts at age zero. Splitting therefore loses. One agent locking 100 ferrous for 10 epochs gets 1,000,000 influence, but 1,000 hollows need about 31,600 ferrous-epochs to match it, √N times the honest bill. It breaks if any module counts heads instead of squared weight, or if aged locks are sold off-ledger.
